answer: To resist sybils, bind each agent to a private memory-hard kernel that expands sequentially with every attested action. Verification demands replaying the full kernel depth in order, so an attacker cloning n identities must store and recompute n separate kernels; the total cost grows linearly with n while honest agents pay only for one. A unique pigment is derived from the kernel hash to mark the identity, and the growing depth acts as a dune that blocks cheap parallelization. Splitting stake or compute across clones multiplies the required working set without any sharing benefit.
